cultivar: Huangshan Gongju, a selection of Chrysanthemum morifolium
processing: Whole flower heads are dried for storage, traditionally by baking at low heat. Little is documented about the exact steps, so ask the seller how a given lot was dried.
harvest_season: Autumn, with the Shexian picking season running into November.
appearance_dry: Small whole flower heads with white petals, a yellow centre and a green calyx.
appearance_wet: The flower heads swell and open in the cup, with soft pale petals around a yellow centre.
taste_profile: Fragrant chrysanthemum with a hint of sweetness and a lingering aftertaste.

brewing.notes: A practical starting point: a small pinch in a glass or lidded mug.

vintage_note: Sold by the autumn harvest, and like other dried flowers it is best drunk fresh rather than aged. Check for a harvest date and avoid lots with a sharp sulphur smell.
description:
Gongju is the small chrysanthemum of Shexian county near Huangshan in southern Anhui, counted among China's four famous chrysanthemums. It contains no tea leaf and no caffeine: the flower is the whole drink.

The flowers are picked in autumn and dried whole. Exact methods are thinly documented, but the look is the thing to know: white petals, yellow heart, green base.

In the cup it is fragrant and lightly sweet, with a lingering finish. A few flowers are enough.

When buying, trust your nose. A pungent sulphur smell is a warning sign. Golden, clear liquor is what a good medicinal-grade chrysanthemum should give.

Chinese tradition treats chrysanthemum as a cooling drink, which is why some people add a few goji berries in autumn.
history:
Accounts from Shexian give the plant more than 800 years of cultivation, and it is now a protected geographical indication of the county. Folk tradition says Huizhou merchants of the Song dynasty brought it from Deqing in Zhejiang as an ornamental flower, and that villagers around Jinzhuling took to drinking it during a year of drought and eye ailments. That story is a legend, not a record.

The variety is still being worked on: growers in Shexian have reported declining quality in the old stock, and a space-seed breeding trial began there in 2025.
